Neha / Marissa — thanks for the heads up, Emma. I've reviewed the Order Form snippets in HubSpot and sketched proposed edits. Summary below; full redline attached.

Key points:
- SCCs: Redwood's standard position is the 2024 SCCs (processor-controller and processor-processor modules as applicable). If GXH insists on 2021 SCCs we can discuss, but the 2024 SCCs are more aligned with our internal compliance tooling.
- Role mapping: I'll produce an Annex A (Processing Activities & Roles) that lists the specific activities (e.g., inference requests, telemetry, support logs), the legal role we assert (Processor), and whether access is required for troubleshooting.
- Subprocessors & TIA: We keep an up-to-date subprocessor list in our compliance portal; for contract execution we'll include an explicit subprocessor locations annex and a TIA template that the customer completes with expected transfer destinations.
- Data export / transfers: Two things to flag — cross-border backups to our eu-central-1 and us-west-2 regions (customer choice), and planned use of an analytics vendor (Optima AI) that stores logs in the US. If GXH is EU-based they may want mitigations; I propose adding optional encryption-at-rest key controls and a right-to-request-local-only processing clause (where feasible).

Attached: Redwood_DPA_Draft_v3.docx (redline), GXH_TIA_template.xlsx (blank TIA), quick subprocessor list stub.

Questions for GXH (to include in the TIA):
1) Which territories do you consider covered by 'EU' for your policies? (EEA only, EEA + UK, or broader)
2) Do you require a controller-controller relationship for any specific processing (e.g., identity verification where you control the dataset)?

I'll wait for Emma's reply and any specific customer redlines.

Hi all — attaching the reviewed redline (see comments in PDF). Short answers to Emma's operational questions:

- Encryption/KMS: Hosted customers: envelope encryption with customer KMS supported via our KMS integration (we document token lifecycle & key rotation limits). Customer-managed keys for full-at-rest control are available only on Dedicated or Private deployments — we'll note that in the DPA.
- Local-only processing: We can commit to regional pinning for inference requests for Dedicated/Private customers; for hosted customers we can include an operational SLA to avoid cross-region processing but cannot guarantee never moving ephemeral backups between zones for DR without Dedicated.
- 2021 vs 2024 SCCs: We'll propose using the 2024 SCCs as the default with an explicit optional clause that allows attaching 2021 SCCs for specific flow annexes if the customer insists — this keeps modern legal alignment while providing flexibility.

Next steps: I will prepare a tracked PDF with line-by-line responses and a DocuSign-ready DPA that reflects the above compromises. Please review the comments and set a time for the Monday call if we need legal-to-legal alignment.

Thanks,
Karthik
